message.content: The kernel uses split-constant range reduction in fp32; for large inputs (|x| up to 65504 is in-domain), the quadrant count q can reach ~41670, so fp32 rounding in q·c and the split-constant approximation can produce errors far above the 1e-6 absolute tolerance. I'll test this directly.

function.arguments: {"statement": "The kernel's fp32 split-constant range reduction produces absolute errors above the 1e-6 contract tolerance for large-magnitude legal FP16 inputs (e.g. near ±65504, where q ≈ 41670).", "rationale": "q·1.5703125 and q·0.000483826... are not exactly representable in fp32 when q is large; accumulated rounding and the missing remainder of π/2 scale with q, so the residual r (and hence the output) drifts by ~q·2⁻²⁴·c, which at q≈4e4 exceeds 1e-6.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_rationale": "The contract states \"EVERY finite FP16 value is legal, including ... both extrema +/-65504\" and requires abs(actual[i]-sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6 throughout the entire legal domain.", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "EVERY finite FP16 value is legal, including both signed zeros, positive and negative subnormal values, and both extrema +/-65504 ... abs(actual[i] - sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6."}]}

message.reasoning_content:
Contract: every finite FP16 value legal, tolerance 1e-6 absolute. This range reduction is classic fdlibm-lite; likely fails badly for large |x| (e.g., ±65504) because q up to ~41670, split-constant reduction error ~q*eps... Actually r_hi = x - q*1.5703125: with q large, catastrophic cancellation? r_hi computed in fp32: x fp32 exact (fp16), q*1.5703125 exact-ish. The residual error accumulates ~q * 2^-something. With q ~ 41670, the reduction constant error 0.000483826... times q gives r error up to ~20, way wrong. Actually the split: π/2 = 1.5703125 + 0.00048382679489661923 + tiny. Sum of those two ≈ 1.57079632679, remainder ~6e-9. So error in r ~ q * 6e-9? No: r = x - q*(c1+c2), missing term c3 ≈ π/2 - 1.5707963267... ≈ tiny. π/2 = 1.5707963267948966. c1+c2 = 1.5707963267948966? 1.5703125+0.00048382679489662 = 1.5707963267948966. So exact double constant. But computation in fp32: q stored fp32 (fine), q*c1 in fp32 has rounding ~1e-7 relative → absolute error in r could be ~ q*c1*2^-24 ≈ 41670*1.57*6e-8 ≈ 0.004. That's > 1e-6. So large inputs fail. Also enable_fp_fusion=False... r_hi = x - q*c1 in fp32: q*1.5703125 exact? 1.5703125 = 1 + 0.5703125, binary exact. q integer up to 41670, product exact in fp32? q*c1 has ~17 bits integer part; c1 has 9 significant bits; product needs ~ up to 26 bits — not exact. So error. Then r_hi - q*c2: c2 has ~24 bits, q large → product rounding.

Plan: record claim, probe with range of inputs including large values.
